rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tells his elite that Moses’ people cannot disrupt the land or escape his rule, using their supposed impotence to excuse his delay in destroying them; qāhir means one who dominates by humiliation.
rows.anchor: اعتذار من فرعون للملإ من قومه عن إبطائه باستئصال موسى وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Above them” is a representational metaphor for being able to subdue them: being elevated over something is the strongest form of power to master it.
rows.anchor: مستعارة لاستطاعة قهرهم لأن الاعتلاء على الشيء أقوى أحوال التمكن من قهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ address to his people answers their response to Pharaoh’s threat (7:125); the dialogue treats him as present, and his words answer Pharaoh by showing disregard for the threat and reliance on God.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { قال موسى لقومه } واقعة جوابا لقول قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s help and being patient together express reliance on God; reliance asks for God’s support toward a desired outcome, is part of seeking help, and entails patience through harm while trusting it will end by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: والتوكل هو جماع قوله : { استعينوا بالله واصبروا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses reassures his people and teaches them that God will grant them victory, which he knows through God’s revelation to him.
rows.anchor: وخاطب موسى قومه بذلك تطمينا لقلوبهم ، وتعليما لهم بنصر الله إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The earth belongs to God” is a concluding rationale for seeking God’s help and patience: unjust rule does not last; the clause is set off because it gives this rationale.
rows.anchor: تذييل وتعليل للأمر بالاستعانة بالله والصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership and inheritance of the earth indirectly signals that Pharaoh’s enslavement will end, countering despair at his visible power: God can grant and remove earthly dominion.
rows.anchor: كناية عن ترقب زوال استعباد فرعون إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The earth” means the world, fitting the general conclusion and rationale; the wording hints that the Israelites will leave Egypt and possess another land.
rows.anchor: فالمراد من الأرض هنا الدنيا لأنه أليق بالتذييل وأقوى في التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The final outcome belongs to the God-fearing” is a concluding statement; the conjunction may be parenthetical and connect this second rationale to seeking God’s help and patience.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { والعاقبة للمتقين } تذييل ، فيجوز أن تكون الواو اعتراضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀqiba literally means the end of a matter; the term appears in 59:17 and 6:11, and prior discussion at 6:11 treats the outcome of deniers.
rows.anchor: والعاقبة حقيقتها نهاية أمر من الأمور وآخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the definite article, ʿāqiba conventionally means an ending better than the beginning, since people prefer their final state to improve; it therefore denotes a pleasing outcome, not an evil one.
rows.anchor: إذا عرفت العاقبة باللام كان المراد منها انتهاء أمر الشيء بأحسن من أوله

rows.speaker: هرقل
rows.claim: In the report of Abū Sufyān, Heraclius says that messengers are tested and then have the favorable outcome.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أبي سفيان قول هرقل : ( وكذلك الرسل تبتلى ثم تكون لهم العاقبة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the final outcome means the Israelites’ worldly outcome, matching the inheritance of the earth, while also including the good outcome in the afterlife, which believers value most.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالعاقبة هنا عاقبة أمورهم في الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing are believers who act.
rows.anchor: والمتقون : المؤمنون العاملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad phrases “whomever He wills of His servants” and “the God-fearing” make both clauses general conclusions and urge listeners to become God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وجيء في جملتي : { إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين } بلفظين عامين ، وهما : من يشاء من عباده والمتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that when the earth has both pious and impious people, God wills the pious to inherit it; rule by others is temporary or reflects equal lack of piety among its people.
rows.anchor: أن من يشاء الله أن يورثهم الأرض هم المتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving the scripture is the messenger’s role; God legislates, while the messenger implements the law and companions and rulers assist its implementation. The messenger’s command also covers those who deputize for him.
rows.anchor: فالله المشرع ، والرسول المنفذ ، وأصحابه وولاة الأمور هم أعوان على التنفيذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command for Moses’ people to take the scripture’s best is for the whole community: “taking” figuratively means adherence and practice, with the preposition indicating attachment.
rows.anchor: تعريج على ما هو حظ عموم الأمة من الشريعة وهو التمسك بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “take it,” taking means receiving and preserving the scripture, a priority for the authority; taking “by” it means adherence and practice, the community’s role.
rows.anchor: لأنه مستعمل في معنى التلقي والحفظ لأنه أهم من الأخذ بمعنى التمسك والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jussive “they take” is the response to the command, expressing certainty that they will comply when ordered.
rows.anchor: وجزم { يأخذوا } جوابا لقوله : { وأمر } تحقيقا لحصول امتثالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Best” is not comparative here but intensifies goodness: it means all the scripture, since its laws are not ranked as better and worse and the community cannot accept only part of the law.
rows.anchor: و { بأحسنها } وصف مسلوب المفاضلة مقصود به المبالغة في الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They took it” repeats the earlier report to express astonishment and to set up the judgment that they were wrongdoers; repetition also emphasizes the point, as in the repeated writing command at 2:282.
rows.anchor: والغرض من التوكيد في مثل هذا المقام هو التكرير لأجل التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They were wrongdoers” is a circumstantial clause modifying the subject of “they took it,” parallel to the wording at 2:51.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { وكانوا ظالمين } في موضع الحال من الضمير المرفوع في قوله : { اتخذوه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You succeeded me” may address Aaron and the leaders, who were Moses’ deputies, and use succession literally.
rows.anchor: وهذا خطاب لهارون ووجوه القوم ، لأنهم خلفاء موسى في قومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it addresses the entire people: Aaron failed to govern them as Moses did, while the people abandoned Moses’ worship of God for the calf, figuratively failing to follow his example.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الخطاب لجميع القوم ، فأما هارون فلأنه لم يحسن الخلافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding “after me” to “you succeeded me” depicts the gulf between them and Moses after his warning against idolatry, including their earlier request for a god like other peoples’ gods.
rows.anchor: وزيادة { من بعدي } عقب { خلفتموني } للتذكير بالبون الشاسع بين حال الخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjila is usually intransitive, meaning to hurry; it can mean failing to complete something begun, or be transitive in the sense of going ahead of something.
rows.anchor: و ( عجل ) أكثر ما يستعمل قاصرا ، بمعنى فعل العجلة أي السرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of “Have you hastened the command of your Lord?” takes command as God’s obligation to preserve the law and await Moses’ return; the people failed to fulfill it and changed things.
rows.anchor: والأمر يكون بمعنى التكليف وهو ما أمرهم الله به : من المحافظة على الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearer reading takes “hastened” as going ahead and “command” as the affair of divine anger and threat: they rushed into the prohibited act soon after warning, as if outrunning punishment; 20:86 is parallel.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو المعنى الأوضح ، ويوضحه قوله ، في نظير هذه القصة في سورة طه ( 86 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses threw the tablets from his hand onto the ground; this indicates they were in his hand when he came down from the divine colloquy, as the Torah explicitly says.
rows.anchor: وذلك يؤذن بأنه لما نزل من المناجاة كانت الألواح في يده كما صرح به في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throwing displayed Moses’ anger or resulted from its surge when he saw the people’s state; the Qur’an mentions it for this significance.
rows.anchor: ثم إن إلقاءه إياها إنما كان إظهارا للغضب ، أو أثرا من آثار فوران الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation that Moses threw the tablets to free his hand to seize Aaron is unsound: it gives the throwing no lesson and the narrative would have used a causal “then.”
rows.anchor: فلا يستقيم قول من فسرها بأن الإلقاء لأجل إشغال يده بجر رأس أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report describes Moses as quick-tempered and severe in anger, linking this to striking the Egyptian and dragging Aaron; his reaction signals the enormity of the people’s deed, not discipline.
rows.anchor: وروي أن موسى عليه السلام كان في خلقه ضيق ، وكان شديدا عند الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Throwing the tablets was not punishment of the people, since tablets containing what would reform them could not appropriately be treated as prophetic discipline.
rows.anchor: وليس تأديبا لهم ، لأنه لا يكون تأديبهم بإلقاء ألواح كتب فيها ما يصلحهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’ apparent view was that Muhammad refrained from writing the final document to discipline the people for disputing in his presence.
rows.anchor: كما هو ظاهر قول ابن عباس ، بل إنما كان ذلك لما رأى من اختلافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that apparent view: Muhammad left the document unwritten because he saw their disagreement and judged it unnecessary for the religion.
rows.anchor: بل إنما كان ذلك لما رأى من اختلافهم في ذلك ، فرأى أن الأولى ترك كتابته

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says the tablets broke when Moses threw them; the Qur’an does not state this, though the act of throwing and a report that they were stone suggest breakage.
rows.anchor: ووقع في التوراة أن الألواح تكسرت حين ألقاها ، وليس في القرآن ما يدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Storytellers invented the claim that six-sevenths of the broken tablets were lost, or that their details vanished while admonition remained; the Qur’an says the tablets still contained guidance and mercy.
rows.anchor: وأما ما روي أنها لما تكسرت ذهب ستة أسباعها ، أو ذهب تفصيلها وبقيت موعظتها ، فهو من وضع القصاصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron’s “they nearly killed me” shows that he resisted them forcefully and then yielded for fear of being killed.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وكادوا يقتلونني } يدل على أنه عارضهم معارضة شديدة ثم سلم خشية القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron’s request not to let enemies gloat or count him among wrongdoers follows his explanation and indirectly asks Moses to refrain from punishing him.
rows.anchor: طلب من أخيه الكف عن عقابه الذي يشمت به الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shamāta is delight at another’s injury, arising from enmity or envy; it is intransitive, has an irregular verbal noun, takes bi for its object, and causative ashmata means to make someone gloat.
rows.anchor: والشماتة : سرور النفس بما يصيب غيرها من الإضرار ، وإنما تحصل من العداوة والحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron’s “enemies” are the calf worshippers who hated him for opposing them; alternatively, their gloating is an idiom for severe harm whether or not enemies exist.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالأعداء الذين دعوا إلى عبادة العجل ، لأن هارون أنكره عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not make me one of the wrongdoers” may mean do not consider me one of them, with “make” meaning “think,” as at 43:19.
rows.anchor: ف ( جعل ) بمعنى ظن كقوله تعالى : { وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عند الرحمن إناثا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Aaron asks not to be punished with the calf worshippers, whom Moses had ordered killed; here “make” retains its basic sense.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : ولا تجعلني في العقوبة معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ prayer answers Aaron. He first asks forgiveness for himself, showing propriety toward God for the anger he displayed, then for his brother in case he was lax in restraining the calf worshippers.
rows.anchor: فطلب المغفرة لنفسه تأدبا مع الله فيما ظهر عليه من الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Aaron “my brother” heightens the appeal for God to forgive him, as Noah invoked his son’s family relation at 11:45.
rows.anchor: وذكر وصف الأخوة هناك زيادة في الاستعطاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering God’s mercy is a metaphor for being enveloped by it in every state, like dwelling in a house; the verb is a primary metaphor and “in” a derivative metaphor replacing association.
rows.anchor: والإدخال في الرحمة استعارة لشمول الرحمة لهما في سائر أحوالهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You are the most merciful of the merciful” concludes the prayer; the conjunction is circumstantial or parenthetical, and the phrase means the greatest in mercy among all who show mercy.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { وأنت أرحم الراحمين } تذييل ، والواو للحال أو اعتراضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes the calf worshippers’ coming punishment through worldly life part of Moses’ speech, received by revelation; it ends with “in worldly life,” after which God’s statement about punishing fabricators is an interjection.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن قوله : { إن الذين اتخذوا العجل } إلى قوله : { الدنيا } من تمام كلام موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, “those who did good” completes the benefit by describing the opposite condition of the people under discussion and their like.
rows.anchor: وأن جملة : { والذين عملوا السيئات } إلى آخر الآية تكملة للفائدة ببيان حالة أضداد المتحدث عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the whole statement about the calf worshippers is God’s answer to Moses’ prayer, with an omitted “We said,” as in God’s answer to Abraham at 2:126.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة : { إن الذين اتخذوا العجل } إلى آخرها خطابا من الله لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanāl means to afflict or reach; its basic sense of taking is metaphorically extended to affliction and involvement, as at 7:37.
rows.anchor: والنول والنيل : الأخذ وهو هنا استعارة للإصابة والتلبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who took the calf are its worshippers; the second object of “took” is omitted for brevity, meaning they took it as a god.
rows.anchor: والذين اتخذوا العجل هم الذين عبدوه فالمفعول الثاني لاتخذوا } محذوف اختصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause identifies the calf worshippers concisely by their known defining act and signals that this act caused their punishment.
rows.anchor: وتعريفهم بطريق الموصولية ، لأنها أخصر طريق في استحضارهم بصفة عرفوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s anger here means its outward effect—abandonment and withholding care—while the anger itself already exists.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالغضب ظهور أثره من الخذلان ومنع العناية ، وأما نفس الغضب فهو حاصل في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine anger means God’s willing harm for a servant and punishing them in this world, the next, or either one.
rows.anchor: وغضب الله تعالى إرادته السوء بعبده وعقابه في الدنيا والآخرة أو في إحداهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhilla is inward abasement from inability to resist: the people become defeated through an enemy’s power, through fear after losing courage, or through alienation from the Holy Land and lifelong homelessness.
rows.anchor: والذلة : خضوع في النفس واستكانة من جراء العجز عن الدفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly humiliation can remain after repentance: repentance removes liability for religious transgression but need not remove worldly consequences, which cease only through special divine favor.
rows.anchor: وهذه الذلة عقوبة دنيوية قد لا تمحوها التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction resembles legal rulings that establish consequences versus obligations, as illustrated by the night-journey report: Gabriel says choosing milk showed guidance to the natural disposition, while wine would have led the community astray.
rows.anchor: وهذا يشبه التفرقة بين خطاب الوضع وخطاب التكليف كما يؤخذ من حديث الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may erase worldly punishment when He is pleased with the offender, for He has great bounty.
rows.anchor: هذا وقد يمحو الله العقوبة الدنيوية إذا رضي عن الجاني والله ذو فضل عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Likewise” means God gives fabricators a punishment like this severe one, as explained at 2:143.
rows.anchor: أي ومثل ذلك الجزاء العظيم نجزي المفترين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iftirāʾ is fabrication without a plausible basis; here it means inventing religious beliefs lacking sound rational or revealed proof, after the Israelites had been warned against idol worship (7:138–140).
rows.anchor: والمراد بالافتراء الاختلاق في أصول الدين بوضع عقائد لا تستند إلى دليل صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author applies the warning historically to Arab polytheists: before Muhammad came they were not humiliated; those who persisted after his guidance were defeated, captured, and dispossessed, while converts gained honor through Islam.
rows.anchor: فلما جاء محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهداهم فاستمروا على الافتراء عاقبهم الله بالذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse yields the general lesson that a liar is cast into humiliation.
rows.anchor: ويؤخذ من هذه الآية أن الكذاب يرمى بالمذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about those who repent interjects a promise after the threat: God forgives by withholding afterlife punishment and ending His anger toward them in the future.
rows.anchor: اعتراض بأنهم إن تابوا وآمنوا يغفر الله لهم على عادة القرآن من تعقيب التهديد بالترغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sins” includes disbelief, the greatest sin, and repentance from disbelief means faith.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسيئات : ما يشمل الكفر ، وهو أعظم السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both instances, “after them” omits a noun supplied by context: after doing the sins, as also with the calf at 2:51.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { من بعدها } في الموضعين حذف مضاف قبل ما أضيفت إليه ( بعد ) وقد شاع حذفه دل عليه { عملوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks a long interval, affirming that repentance remains accepted even after a long period filled with sins.
rows.anchor: وحرف ( ثم ) هنا مفيد للتراخي ، وذلك إلجاء إلى قبول التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated “after them” further stresses the interval and implies to polytheists that conversion will be forgiven even after a long period of idolatry.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لمفاد المهلة التي أفادها حرف ( ثم ) وهذا تعريض للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is conjoined with repentance either to emphasize that faith grounds acceptance of good deeds and prevent doubt that repentance can cure idolatry, or because it means sincere faith inclusive of duties.
rows.anchor: وعطف الإيمان على التوبة ، مع أن التوبة تشمله من حيث إن الإيمان توبة من الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord” most likely addresses Muhammad; alternatively, it addresses Moses if the prior statement about the calf worshippers was God’s speech to him.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في قوله : { إن ربك } لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم على الوجه الأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive “your” honors the one addressed as God’s servant, and mentioning lordship prepares for the attribute of mercy.
rows.anchor: وفي تعريف المسند إليه بالإضافة توسل إلى تشريف المضاف إليه
